title: About
text:
I am a PhD Candidate (ABD) in Biostatistics and Data Analytics at Florida International University (FIU) in Miami, Florida.
My research interests span methodological and applied biostatistics, with particular interests in regression modeling, statistical inference, multicollinearity, shrinkage estimation, survival analysis, epidemiology, causal inference, clinical research, and machine learning for health data.
My work combines statistical methodology, Monte Carlo simulation, computational statistics, and applications to biomedical and public health research.

title: Research
text: My research spans methodological statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology, and health data science. I am particularly interested in developing and evaluating statistical methods and applying them to complex biomedical and public health data.

title: Research
text:
Methodological Research
My methodological research focuses on regression modeling, statistical inference, multicollinearity, shrinkage estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation.
Current and previous work includes:

Development and evaluation of one- and two-parameter regression estimators under multicollinearity
Empirical comparison of Type I error and statistical power
Ridge regression and Liu-type estimators
Elastic Net and robust estimation methods
Monte Carlo simulation studies
Applications of statistical methodology to real-world datasets

title: Research
text:
Biomedical & Public Health Research
I collaborate on interdisciplinary research involving:

Maternal and neonatal health
Oncology and fertility preservation
HIV/AIDS and COVID-19
Alzheimer’s disease
Environmental and climate health
Population health

title: Research
text:
Survival Analysis & Machine Learning
My work with longitudinal Alzheimer’s disease data includes prediction of progression from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia.
Methods include:

Cox proportional hazards models
Multi-state survival analysis
LASSO regression
DeepSurv neural networks
Longitudinal risk prediction
Biomarker evaluation

title: Research
text:
Environmental & Epidemiologic Methods
My collaborative research has involved statistical analysis of environmental exposures and health outcomes using methods including:

Logistic regression
Weighted Quantile Sum (WQS) regression
Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression (BKMR)
Structural Equation Modeling (SEM)
Multiple imputation
Sensitivity analysis

title: Research
text:
Research Goal
My broader research goal is to develop statistically rigorous and computationally useful methods that can improve analysis and decision-making in biomedical, clinical, and public health research.

title: Selected Projects
section: Machine Learning for Breast Cancer Diagnosis

Machine Learning for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
Applied machine learning methods to breast cancer diagnosis data for classification and predictive modeling.
Methods: Machine Learning · Classification · Predictive Modeling

title: Selected Projects
text:
Alzheimer’s Disease Progression Modeling
Developed survival and machine-learning models using longitudinal Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) data to study progression from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia.
Methods: Cox Regression · Multi-State Survival Analysis · LASSO · DeepSurv · Machine Learning

title: Selected Projects
text:
Environmental Exposures and Maternal Health
Analyzed associations between environmental metal mixtures and maternal/neonatal health outcomes.
Methods: Logistic Regression · WQS Regression · BKMR · Structural Equation Modeling

title: Selected Projects
text:
HIV and COVID-19 Research
Contributed to epidemiological studies involving HIV/AIDS and COVID-19, including research on excess mortality among people with HIV in Florida during the early COVID-19 period.
Methods: Epidemiologic Analysis · Farrington Algorithm · Regression Modeling
